## TRA Timeline

#### SciPlay Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2019-05-07: TRA executed concurrent with SciPlay Up-C IPO; SciPlay Corporation (obligor) and SG Social Holding Company I and II (Scientific Games subsidiaries; later renamed LNW Social Holding I and II) as beneficiaries
- 2019-05-08: 8-K Item 1.01 files the executed TRA as Exhibit 10.1

#### Corporate rebrand

- 2022-03: Scientific Games Corporation rebrands to Light & Wonder, Inc.; same CIK; SG Social Holding entities rename to LNW Social Holding I and II; no TRA amendment

#### SciPlay take-private and Section 4.1(b) waivers

- 2023-08-08: Merger Agreement signed for Light & Wonder to acquire SciPlay public minority; no TRA waivers at signing
- 2023-10-23: Merger closes; three Section 4.1(b) waivers executed (one each by SciPlay Corporation, SciPlay Parent Company LLC, and LNW Social Holding Company I); waivers decline change-of-control acceleration while preserving the TRA in force
- 2023+: Post-merger TRA payments continue but are intercompany and eliminated in consolidation

## Explanation

Scientific Games Corporation (renamed Light & Wonder, Inc. in March 2022) is the beneficiary side of a single TRA executed May 7, 2019 at the SciPlay Corporation Up-C IPO, under which SciPlay (the issuer) pays 85% of cash tax savings from IPO-time basis step-ups, exchange-driven basis step-ups, and TRA-payment-derived basis to two Scientific Games subsidiaries (renamed LNW Social Holding Company I and II after the rebrand). On October 23, 2023, Light & Wonder closed a take-private merger for SciPlay's public minority; rather than terminating the TRA via a separate instrument, the three parties each delivered a Section 4.1(b) waiver declining the change-of-control acceleration while expressly stating the TRA remains in full force and effect. The TRA now operates entirely intercompany within the Light & Wonder consolidated group, so payments are eliminated in consolidation and post-2023 10-Ks carry no TRA disclosure; pre-merger payments included $4M for fiscal 2022. The contract could re-emerge as a separate-entity obligation only if Light & Wonder spun off, sold, or re-IPO'd SciPlay. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
